back: The overall structure of a system: components, layers or tiers, their responsibilities and how they communicate.
Presentation (shows and collects), logic (applies the rules), data (stores and retrieves).
A client requests a service from a server that provides it (for example a browser and a web server).
Benefits: logic in one place, database hidden, tiers scale separately. Drawbacks: more computers, delay, complexity.
The operations a component offers to others; they need not know how it works inside.
Each layer has one responsibility and uses only the layer below, so one layer can change without the others.
A layer is a logical division of the design; a tier is a layer deployed on its own computer.
Choose the simplest design that meets the requirements: users, security, location, how often the logic changes.
Servers = peak requests per second ÷ requests one server can process per second, rounded up.
